title: Mass spectrometry-based proteomic analysis of NSCLC tumor and biopsy samples
protocol: Add four volumes of ice-cold acetone relative to the sample volume to each protein fraction from the Allprep kit.
Invert the tubes three times and incubate at -20°C for 60 min.
Centrifuge the samples for 10 min at 12,000 × g in a pre-cooled centrifuge at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and wash the pellet once with 100 μl of ice-cold ethanol.
Disperse the pellet in 100 μl ice-cold ethanol by ultrasonication (Program: Am 50%, time 10 s, pulse 1.0 s).
Centrifuge the samples again.
Air-dry the resulting pellet for 10 min.
Dissolve the pellet in 200 μl of reconstitution buffer (4% w/v SDS, 25 mM HEPES pH 7.6).
Mix 1 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) with the reconstituted protein sample.
Add chloroacetamide to achieve a final concentration of 4–10 mM for alkylation.
Capture proteins on SP3 beads by adding stock bead suspension at a ratio of 1:10 to the sample volume and adding acetonitrile (ACN) for a final concentration of 70%.
Incubate the mixture under rotation for 30 minutes at room temperature (RT).
Place tubes on a magnetic rack and incubate for 2 minutes at RT to remove lysis buffer.
Discard supernatant and remove tubes from the magnetic rack.
Wash bead-attached-proteins twice with 500 μl of 70% ethanol, incubating each wash for 30 seconds on the magnetic rack followed by removal of the supernatant.
Add 200 μl of ACN to the samples and incubate for 15 seconds on the magnetic rack.
Discard the supernatant and air-dry the beads for 30 seconds.
Digest proteins sequentially with LysC and trypsin enzymes at 37 °C for a minimum of 20 hours.
Prepare the first digestion solution containing LysC in 1 M Urea/50 mM HEPES (enzyme to protein ratio of 1:50).
Add trypsin in 50 mM HEPES to the digestion solution after the initial enzyme reaction (enzyme to protein ratio of 1:50).
Collect digested peptides as supernatant after placing the tube on a magnetic rack.
Add 50 μl of water twice to collect remaining peptides.
Measure peptide concentration using Bio-Rad DC protein assay.
Exclude samples with insufficient peptide amount (<100 µg) for TMT labeling.
Pre-screen remaining samples by LC-MS/MS using short-gradient DDA runs (60 min).
Identify and exclude outlier samples based on analysis of the short-gradient data.
Exclude 10 samples due to extensive blood contamination from MS data.
Re-analyze clinical data post-MS data generation.
Exclude two additional samples with uncertain primary tumor origin after MS data generation.
Prepare a reference pool before TMT labeling to function as denominator in each TMT set.
Pool peptides from AC samples to form a 1-mg sub-pool.
Pool peptides from SqCC samples to form a 1-mg sub-pool.
Pool peptides from LCC and LCNEC samples to form a 1-mg sub-pool.
Combine the three sub-pools to create a final 3-mg reference pool.
Label 100 μg of peptides from each tumor sample and reference pool with TMT 10-plex reagent according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Distribute labeled samples across 16 TMT sets, including one reference pool per set except for the last set which includes two reference pools.
Prepare an additional TMT set (No. 17) with four reference pool samples and six tumor sample replicates also present in primary sets.
Pool labeled samples from each TMT set together.
Clean pooled labeled samples by strata-X-C-cartridges and dry in a vacuum centrifuge.
Separate TMT-labeled peptides using High-Resolution Isoelectric Focusing (HiRIEF) on pH 3.7–4.9 strips.
Extract peptides from HiRIEF strips using Etan digester (modified Gilson liquid handler).
Put a polypropylene well-former with 72 wells onto each strip.
Add 50 μl of MilliQ water to each well.
Incubate for 30 minutes.
Transfer the liquid from each well to a V-bottom, polypropylene 96-well plate.
Repeat extraction twice more using 35% ACN and then 35% ACN/0.1% formic acid in MilliQ water.
Dry the extracted peptides in the 96-well plate using a SpeedVac.
Dispense 20 μl of 3% ACN/0.1% FA solvent into each well of the microtiter plate using an autosampler.
Mix by aspirating and dispensing 10 μl ten times.
Inject 10 μl into a C18 trap desalting column (Acclaim pepmap, C18, 3 µm bead size, 100 Å, 75 μm x 20 mm).
Separate peptides using a gradient of mobile phase A and B from 6% to 37% B over 30-90 minutes.
Operate the Q Exactive HF in data-dependent acquisition mode.
Select top 5 precursors for fragmentation by high-energy collision dissociation (HCD).
Perform survey scans at 60,000 resolution from 300-1500 m/z.
Aliquot peptide samples prior to TMT-labeling for the early-stage cohort.
Undergo an additional SP3 peptide clean-up step for each of the peptide samples from the early-stage cohort.
Obtain 450 µl of protein extract using the AllPrep Kit for late-stage cohort samples.
Use 225 µl of protein extract for further processing in the late-stage cohort.
Cut tumor pieces to obtain a 2 × 2 mm slice for the validation cohort.
Wash each tumor piece thrice with PBS (1 ml) for the validation cohort.
Homogenize and lyse tissue pieces in 200 μl of lysis buffer using Precellys lysing kit “Tissue homogenizing CKMix” tubes for the validation cohort.
Heat samples on a shaker at 95 °C, 500 rpm for 5 minutes.
Sonicate samples with 50% amplitude in 1-second pulses for 1 minute.
Transfer protein extracts to Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 14,000 × g for 15 minutes.
Repeat centrifugation and tube transfer until debris is completely removed.
Measure total protein concentration using the Bio-Rad DC protein assay kit.
Aliquot 200 μg of protein for further processing in the validation cohort.
Use the entire sample for the late-stage cohort.
Perform SP3 protein clean-up and digestion as described for early-stage samples.
Incubate SP3 bead suspension (10 μg/μl, 1:10 ratio) with ACN and peptides at room temperature for 30 minutes under rotation.
Place tubes on a magnetic rack; discard supernatant and wash beads twice with 200 µl of ACN.
Air-dry the SP3 beads briefly.
Elute peptides using 100 μl of 3% ACN/0.1% FA solution.
Transfer eluted peptides to new tubes.
Measure peptide concentration using the Bio-Rad DC protein assay kit.
Combine peptides from 129 different tumor samples for spectral library generation.
Aliquot 2 mg of pooled peptides into two parts.
Subject each part of the pooled peptides to fractionation, one by HiRIEF and one by high-pH peptide fractionation.
Separate peptides by IPG-IEF on pH 3–10 strips using HiRIEF pre-fractionation method.
Dry extracted peptides in SpeedVac.
Dissolve dried peptides in 3% ACN/0.1% FA.
Consolidate to a final of 40 fractions as described in the HiRIEF fraction scheme file.
Load peptides onto a 25 cm C18 packed column for high-pH peptide fractionation using BPRP HPLC.
Collect 96 fractions from the column and consolidate to a final of 40 fractions.
Trap samples on an Acclaim PepMap nanotrap column.
Separate peptides using an Acclaim PepMap RSLC column.
Use mobile phase A (5% DMSO, 0.1% FA) and B (90% ACN, 5% DMSO, 0.1% FA).
Apply a gradient from 6% to 30% B over 180 minutes with a flow rate of 250 nl/min.
Analyze each fraction using data-dependent acquisition (DDA) for selecting top 10 precursors for fragmentation by HCD.
Perform survey scans at 120,000 resolution from 400 to 1200 m/z with a max injection time of 100 ms and target of 1 × 10^6 ions.
Generate HCD fragmentation spectra with a max ion injection time of 100 ms and AGC of 2 × 10^5 before fragmentation at 25% normalized collision energy, 30,000 resolution.
Isolate precursors with a width of 2 m/z and put them on the exclusion list for 15 seconds.
Reject single and unassigned charge states from precursor selection.
Dissolve samples in phase A (5% DMSO, 0.1% FA).
Inject 5 μg of peptides into the LC-MS system.
Acquire data using a variable window strategy with survey scans at 120,000 resolution from 400 to 1200 m/z and max injection time of 200 ms and target of 1 × 10^6 ions.
